thread:
maya: Quick callout 1: mixed tiny+huge requests keep causing evictions and tiny req p99 spikes. Thinking: mark tiny requests at enqueue as 'drain_protected' and give a short drain window (4-12ms) vs tuning soft-evict. Thoughts?

lee: I'm intrigued. 'drain_protected' seems low risk if feature-flagged. Avoids cross-batcher complexity.

anil: How do we define tiny? token_count < 64? Also need fallback so reservations don't stall big bursts.

maya: Proposal: small_token_cutoff=64, drain_window_ms=8, enabled=auto (turns on only when small_req_ratio > 0.1). Circuit: if queueing > 50ms fall back to soft-evict.

rachel: Telemetry must include protected_evictions, small_req_p99, gpu_util, and cost delta per GPU-hour. We'll need those for canary.

tim: Watch kv-cache warmup interaction. If protecting tiny reqs prevents warmup for subsequent big requests, we could regress throughput/cost. Add a kv_warmup_delta metric.

maya: Plan: lee to implement enqueue-flag prototype behind flag; rachel to add dash; tim to add queue-depth circuit-breaker. Run canary on 3 low-traffic hosts.

canary-bot: deploy: Canary started for flag batcher.drain_protect=on (hosts: canary-3).

lee: I'll open a small PR and include tests for no-regression when QPS is low.

maya: Thanks everyone. If the canary shows <5% throughput loss and p99 improvement for tiny reqs, we can iterate to adaptive sizing. :thumbsup:
